goal:
Build an ORDERS feature for this Vite + React 19 + TypeScript store, wired into the existing app. No new runtime dependencies (vitest may be added as a dev dependency). Strict TypeScript, no `any`, JSDoc on every export, `npm run build` must pass and `npx vitest run` must be green.

1. src/orders/types.ts — the domain: `Order`, `OrderLine`, `OrderStatus` ("pending" | "paid" | "shipped" | "delivered" | "cancelled"), `Address`, `PaymentMethod`, `OrderError` (a typed Error subclass with a `code` of "declined" | "out_of_stock" | "network"), and `OrderDraft` (what the UI holds before submission).
2. src/orders/api.ts — a mock backend over a seeded in-memory store: `listOrders()`, `getOrder(id)`, `placeOrder(draft)`, `cancelOrder(id)`, `advanceOrder(id)` (pending→paid→shipped→delivered). Every call returns a Promise resolving after 50–150 ms; `placeOrder` rejects with OrderError("declined") when the card number ends in "0000" and OrderError("out_of_stock") when a line's qty exceeds 10. Ids are `ORD-<8 uppercase base36>`, stable and unique.
3. src/orders/storage.ts — orders persist to localStorage under "ministore:orders" through a versioned envelope, validated on load (drop malformed orders, clamp line quantities to 1..99, unknown status → "pending"), with `loadOrders()`, `saveOrders(orders)` and `clearOrders()`.
4. src/orders/totals.ts — pure money maths over an order: `subtotal(order)`, `shipping(order)` (free over $50, else $7.99), `tax(order, rate)` (rounded to the cent, half-up), `total(order)`, and `formatOrderTotal(order, locale)` via Intl.NumberFormat. All amounts are whole dollars in `Product.price`, as the existing catalogue has them.
5. src/orders/status.ts — the state machine: `canTransition(from, to)`, `nextStatus(current)`, `isTerminal(status)`, `statusLabel(status)` (human wording) and `transitionsFor(status)` (what the UI may offer). Cancelled and delivered are terminal; nothing moves backwards.
6. src/orders/useOrders.ts — the React hook binding the pieces: `orders`, `loading`, `error`, `place(draft)`, `cancel(id)`, `advance(id)`, `refresh()`; it loads from storage on mount, writes through on every change, surfaces OrderError by code, and never leaves `loading` stuck after a rejection.
7. src/orders/OrdersPage.tsx — the screen: a list of orders (id, date, status pill, total, line count), an empty state, a detail panel for the selected order showing its lines and the totals breakdown, and per-order actions driven by `transitionsFor` (Cancel, Advance) with the buttons disabled while a call is in flight.
8. src/orders/OrderRow.tsx — the row component used by the page: props `{ order, selected, onSelect, onCancel, onAdvance, busy }`, keyboard accessible (Enter/Space selects), with the status pill coloured per status.
9. Wire it in: a "Orders" button in the existing header of src/App.tsx toggles between the store page and OrdersPage; placing an order from the existing cart drawer (the Checkout button) creates an order through `useOrders().place` and clears the cart. The store page must keep working exactly as it does now.
10. Tests (vitest, jsdom not required): at least 40 unit tests across api (ids, delays, both rejection paths), storage (round trip, corrupt store, clamping, unknown status), totals (each function, the free-shipping boundary, tax rounding), status (every legal and illegal transition, terminals) and useOrders' pure helpers. `npx vitest run` must be green.
11. README.md — an "Orders" section: the storage key, the status machine, the shipping and tax rules, and how to run the tests.

blueprint.summary: Add a self-contained src/orders/ feature (domain types, mock API, localStorage persistence, money/status logic, a useOrders hook, and two components) and wire an Orders toggle + real checkout into src/App.tsx.

modules.purpose: Domain types and error class shared by every other orders module.

exports.name: OrderStatus
exports.doc: The lifecycle stage of an order.

acceptance.text: OrderStatus is exactly the 5-member string union; assigning any other string literal to a variable typed OrderStatus is a compile error.

exports.name: OrderLine
exports.signature: export type OrderLine = { productId: string; name: string; price: number; qty: number };
exports.doc: One product and quantity captured inside an order or draft. price is the whole-dollar unit price at the time of the line, independent of the live catalogue.

acceptance.text: All four fields are required; omitting any one (e.g. `{ productId: "mug", name: "Stone mug", price: 18 }` with qty missing) is a compile error.

exports.name: Address
exports.signature: export type Address = { name: string; street: string; city: string; postalCode: string; country: string };
exports.doc: Shipping address for an order.

acceptance.text: All five fields are required string fields.

exports.name: PaymentMethod
exports.signature: export type PaymentMethod = { cardNumber: string; expiry: string; nameOnCard: string };
exports.doc: Card details captured for an order; cardNumber is the raw digit string used only by the mock backend's decline check.

acceptance.text: All three fields are required string fields.

exports.name: Order
exports.signature: export type Order = { id: string; createdAt: string; status: OrderStatus; lines: OrderLine[]; address: Address; payment: PaymentMethod };
exports.doc: A placed order as stored and displayed. id matches /^ORD-[0-9A-Z]{8}$/, createdAt is an ISO-8601 timestamp string.

acceptance.text: id and createdAt are string, status is OrderStatus, lines is OrderLine[]; a value missing `status` fails to typecheck as Order.

exports.name: OrderDraft
exports.signature: export type OrderDraft = { lines: OrderLine[]; address: Address; payment: PaymentMethod };
exports.doc: What the UI assembles before calling placeOrder; same shape as Order minus id/createdAt/status, which the backend assigns.

acceptance.text: OrderDraft has no `id`, `createdAt` or `status` field — assigning an Order value where an OrderDraft is expected still typechecks (Order is a superset) but the reverse (OrderDraft where Order is expected) is a compile error.

exports.name: OrderErrorCode
exports.doc: The reason an order operation failed.

acceptance.text: OrderErrorCode is exactly this 3-member union.

exports.name: OrderError
exports.doc: Typed error thrown/rejected by api.ts. message defaults to a human-readable phrase for the code when omitted. Must not use TS parameter-property shorthand in the constructor (erasableSyntaxOnly forbids it) — assign `this.code` in the body instead.

acceptance.text: `new OrderError("declined") instanceof Error` is true and `.code === "declined"`.
`new OrderError("out_of_stock", "only 3 left").message === "only 3 left"`.
`new OrderError("network").message` is a non-empty string (the default).

modules.purpose: Mock backend: a seeded in-memory Order store with delayed, sometimes-failing Promise calls.

exports.name: generateOrderId
exports.doc: Produces an id of the form ORD-<8 uppercase base36 chars>, unique per call.

acceptance.text: generateOrderId() matches /^ORD-[0-9A-Z]{8}$/.
Calling generateOrderId() 1000 times yields 1000 distinct values (Set size 1000).

exports.name: listOrders
exports.doc: Resolves with every order currently in the mock store, after a 50–150 ms delay. The store seeds with exactly 2 demo orders on module load.

acceptance.text: A fresh import's first listOrders() call resolves to an array of length 2.
The elapsed time between calling listOrders() and its resolution is between 50 ms and 200 ms (allowing test-timer slack above the 150 ms nominal ceiling).

exports.name: getOrder
exports.signature: export function getOrder(id: string): Promise<Order | undefined>
exports.doc: Resolves with the matching order, or undefined if no order with that id exists, after a 50–150 ms delay.

acceptance.text: getOrder(id) for an id returned by a prior placeOrder() resolves to an order with that same id.
getOrder("ORD-NOPE0000") resolves to undefined.

exports.name: placeOrder
exports.doc: Validates and stores a new order with status "pending". Rejects with OrderError("declined") when draft.payment.cardNumber ends in "0000" (checked first); otherwise rejects with OrderError("out_of_stock") when any line's qty exceeds 10. On success the resolved Order's id is a freshly generated id and it is appended to the in-memory store.

acceptance.text: placeOrder with cardNumber "4242424242420000" and valid lines rejects with an OrderError whose code is "declined".
placeOrder with a valid card and a line of qty 11 rejects with an OrderError whose code is "out_of_stock".
placeOrder with cardNumber ending "0000" AND a line of qty 11 rejects with code "declined" (decline check runs first).
placeOrder with a valid card and all line qty <= 10 resolves to an Order with status "pending", an id matching /^ORD-[0-9A-Z]{8}$/, and lines equal to draft.lines.
After a successful placeOrder, a subsequent listOrders() includes the new order's id.

exports.name: cancelOrder
exports.doc: Sets the order's status to "cancelled" and resolves with the updated order. Rejects with a plain Error if the id is unknown or the order is already terminal (isTerminal true).

acceptance.text: cancelOrder on a freshly placed ("pending") order resolves to an Order with status "cancelled".
cancelOrder("ORD-NOPE0000") rejects.
Calling cancelOrder twice on the same id (second call after the order is already cancelled) rejects on the second call.

exports.name: advanceOrder
exports.doc: Moves the order to nextStatus(order.status) and resolves with the updated order. Rejects with a plain Error if the id is unknown or the order is terminal (nextStatus would be null).

acceptance.text: Three sequential advanceOrder calls on a newly placed order move its status pending -> paid -> shipped -> delivered in order.
advanceOrder on a delivered order rejects.
advanceOrder on a cancelled order rejects.
advanceOrder("ORD-NOPE0000") rejects.

modules.purpose: Versioned, validated read/write of the order list to localStorage.

exports.name: STORAGE_KEY
exports.doc: localStorage key under which the versioned orders envelope is stored.

acceptance.text: STORAGE_KEY === "ministore:orders".

exports.name: loadOrders
exports.doc: Reads and parses the STORAGE_KEY envelope. Returns [] if the key is absent, the JSON is invalid, or the envelope shape is wrong. Drops any order missing a required field (id, createdAt, status, lines, address, payment) or with a wrong-typed one. For surviving orders, clamps every line's qty into 1..99 and replaces an unrecognized status string with "pending".

acceptance.text: With nothing at STORAGE_KEY, loadOrders() returns [].
With STORAGE_KEY set to a non-JSON string, loadOrders() returns [].
Given a valid envelope containing one well-formed order and one order missing `address`, loadOrders() returns an array of length 1 (the malformed one is dropped).
Given a well-formed order with a line qty of 0, loadOrders() returns that order with the line's qty clamped to 1.
Given a well-formed order with a line qty of 500, loadOrders() returns that order with the line's qty clamped to 99.
Given a well-formed order whose status is "refunded" (not a real OrderStatus), loadOrders() returns that order with status "pending".

exports.name: saveOrders
exports.doc: Writes { version, orders } as JSON to STORAGE_KEY, overwriting any existing value.

acceptance.text: After saveOrders([o]) then loadOrders(), the result is an array containing an order with the same id as o (round trip).

exports.name: clearOrders
exports.doc: Removes STORAGE_KEY from localStorage entirely.

acceptance.text: After saveOrders([o]) then clearOrders(), loadOrders() returns [].

modules.purpose: Pure money math over an Order, in whole-dollar units matching Product.price.

exports.name: subtotal
exports.doc: Sum of line.price * line.qty across order.lines.

acceptance.text: For an order with lines [{price:18,qty:2},{price:64,qty:1}] (other fields aside), subtotal(order) === 100.
For an order with lines: [], subtotal(order) === 0.

exports.name: shipping
exports.doc: 0 when subtotal(order) >= 50, otherwise 7.99 (the free-shipping threshold is inclusive of $50 exactly).

acceptance.text: For an order whose subtotal is 49, shipping(order) === 7.99.
For an order whose subtotal is 50, shipping(order) === 0.
For an order whose subtotal is 51, shipping(order) === 0.

exports.name: tax
exports.signature: export function tax(order: Order, rate: number): number
exports.doc: subtotal(order) * rate, rounded to the nearest cent, half-up (ties round away from zero). Shipping is not taxed.

acceptance.text: For an order with subtotal 1 and rate 0.125, tax(order, 0.125) === 0.13 (0.125 rounds half-up to 0.13).
For an order with subtotal 100 and rate 0.0825, tax(order, 0.0825) === 8.25.

exports.name: total
exports.doc: subtotal(order) + shipping(order). Excludes tax, since total takes no rate parameter.

acceptance.text: For an order with subtotal 30 (shipping 7.99), total(order) === 37.99.
For an order with subtotal 50 (shipping 0), total(order) === 50.

exports.name: formatOrderTotal
exports.signature: export function formatOrderTotal(order: Order, locale: string): string
exports.doc: Formats total(order) as USD currency via `new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: "currency", currency: "USD" })`.

acceptance.text: For an order whose total is 37.99, formatOrderTotal(order, "en-US") === "$37.99".

modules.purpose: The order status state machine: legal transitions, terminality, and display labels.

exports.name: transitionsFor
exports.doc: The statuses the UI may offer from the current one: pending -> [paid, cancelled]; paid -> [shipped, cancelled]; shipped -> [delivered, cancelled]; delivered -> []; cancelled -> [].

acceptance.text: transitionsFor("pending") equals ["paid","cancelled"] (order-insensitive set equality).
transitionsFor("paid") equals ["shipped","cancelled"].
transitionsFor("shipped") equals ["delivered","cancelled"].
transitionsFor("delivered") equals [].
transitionsFor("cancelled") equals [].

exports.name: canTransition
exports.signature: export function canTransition(from: OrderStatus, to: OrderStatus): boolean
exports.doc: True iff `to` is a member of transitionsFor(from).

acceptance.text: canTransition("pending", "paid") === true.
canTransition("pending", "shipped") === false (cannot skip a step).
canTransition("paid", "pending") === false (no backwards transitions).
canTransition("delivered", "cancelled") === false (delivered is terminal).
canTransition("cancelled", "pending") === false (cancelled is terminal).

exports.name: nextStatus
exports.signature: export function nextStatus(current: OrderStatus): OrderStatus | null
exports.doc: The single-step advance target: pending->paid, paid->shipped, shipped->delivered; null for delivered and cancelled.

acceptance.text: nextStatus("pending") === "paid"; nextStatus("paid") === "shipped"; nextStatus("shipped") === "delivered".
nextStatus("delivered") === null and nextStatus("cancelled") === null.

exports.name: isTerminal
exports.doc: True for "delivered" and "cancelled", false for the other three statuses.

acceptance.text: isTerminal("delivered") === true and isTerminal("cancelled") === true.
isTerminal("pending") === false, isTerminal("paid") === false, isTerminal("shipped") === false.

exports.name: statusLabel
exports.doc: Human-readable label: "Pending", "Paid", "Shipped", "Delivered", "Cancelled".

acceptance.text: statusLabel("pending") === "Pending"; statusLabel("cancelled") === "Cancelled".

modules.purpose: React hook binding api.ts + storage.ts into the state the UI renders; exposes its state-merge logic as pure, independently testable helpers.
imports: import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { listOrders, placeOrder, cancelOrder, advanceOrder } from "./api";

exports.name: upsertOrder
exports.signature: export function upsertOrder(orders: Order[], updated: Order): Order[]
exports.doc: Returns a new array: if an order with updated.id already exists, it is replaced in place at the same index; otherwise updated is appended. Does not mutate orders.

acceptance.text: upsertOrder([a, b], updatedA) where updatedA.id === a.id returns [updatedA, b] (b unchanged, a replaced in place).
upsertOrder([a], c) where c.id is not a.id returns [a, c].
upsertOrder([a, b], updatedA) does not mutate the original input array (original array's first element is still the original a).

exports.name: toOrderError
exports.doc: Normalizes any thrown/rejected value into an OrderError: an OrderError is returned as-is; an Error is wrapped as OrderError("network", err.message); anything else is wrapped as OrderError("network", String(err)).

acceptance.text: toOrderError(new OrderError("declined", "x")) returns a value with code "declined" and message "x".
toOrderError(new Error("boom")) returns an OrderError with code "network" and message "boom".
toOrderError("oops") returns an OrderError with code "network" and message "oops".

exports.name: UseOrdersResult
exports.signature: export type UseOrdersResult = { orders: Order[]; loading: boolean; error: OrderError | null; place: (draft: OrderDraft) => Promise<Order>; cancel: (id: string) => Promise<void>; advance: (id: string) => Promise<void>; refresh: () => Promise<void> };
exports.doc: The shape returned by useOrders().

acceptance.text: OrdersPage.tsx can destructure { orders, loading, error, place, cancel, advance, refresh } from a UseOrdersResult without a type error.

exports.name: useOrders
exports.doc: On mount, initializes `orders` synchronously from loadOrders(). Every change to `orders` is written through to storage via saveOrders(). place/cancel/advance call the matching api.ts function, merge the result into `orders` via upsertOrder, and set `loading` true for the call's duration and false again whether it resolves or rejects. A rejection is normalized with toOrderError and stored in `error`; a subsequent successful call clears `error`. refresh() calls api.listOrders() and replaces `orders` wholesale.

acceptance.text: Return type matches UseOrdersResult exactly; a component may call `const { orders, loading, error, place, cancel, advance, refresh } = useOrders();` and pass `orders` where Order[] is expected.
`loading` is never left true after place/cancel/advance rejects — implemented via try/finally (or equivalent) around each call.
On mount, before any api call resolves, `orders` already equals loadOrders()'s synchronous result (instant paint from the local cache).

modules.purpose: One selectable, keyboard-accessible row in the orders list, with a status pill and per-row actions.

exports.name: OrderRowProps
exports.signature: export type OrderRowProps = { order: Order; selected: boolean; onSelect: (id: string) => void; onCancel: (id: string) => void; onAdvance: (id: string) => void; busy: boolean };
exports.doc: Props for OrderRow: onSelect/onCancel/onAdvance receive order.id; busy disables the action buttons while a call for this order is in flight.

acceptance.text: OrdersPage.tsx can construct a valid OrderRowProps object and pass it to <OrderRow ...> without a type error.

exports.name: OrderRow
exports.signature: export default function OrderRow(props: OrderRowProps): JSX.Element
exports.doc: Renders the order's id, date (order.createdAt), a status pill (colour keyed off order.status, labelled via statusLabel), total (via totals.total/formatOrderTotal) and line count. The row is focusable (tabIndex 0, role="button") and calls onSelect(order.id) on click, Enter, or Space. Cancel/Advance buttons are shown per transitionsFor(order.status) and disabled while props.busy is true.

acceptance.text: Component compiles against OrderRowProps with no `any` and satisfies erasableSyntaxOnly/verbatimModuleSyntax.
Pressing Enter or Space while the row is focused invokes onSelect(order.id); other keys do not.
Cancel/Advance buttons are rendered disabled when props.busy is true.

modules.purpose: The Orders screen: list + empty state + selected-order detail panel with totals breakdown.
imports: import { subtotal, shipping, tax, total, formatOrderTotal } from "./totals";

exports.name: OrdersPage
exports.doc: Calls useOrders() and renders: an empty state when orders.length === 0; otherwise a list of OrderRow, one per order, tracking a selected id in local state. The selected order's lines and totals breakdown (subtotal/shipping/tax/total via totals.ts) render in a detail panel. Each row's Cancel/Advance handlers call useOrders().cancel/advance and pass `busy` while that order's call is pending.

acceptance.text: Component compiles with no `any`, respecting verbatimModuleSyntax and erasableSyntaxOnly.
With orders.length === 0, an empty-state message is rendered instead of a list.
Selecting a row shows that order's lines and a totals breakdown (subtotal, shipping, tax, total) in the detail panel.
Only the transitions returned by transitionsFor(order.status) are offered as buttons for that row/detail.

modules.purpose: Add an Orders toggle to the header and make the cart's Checkout button place a real order via useOrders().place before clearing the cart.
imports: import { products, formatPrice, type Product } from "./products";

exports.name: App
exports.doc: Adds a `view` state ("store" | "orders") and an "Orders" nav button that toggles it, rendering OrdersPage in place of the product grid + hero when view is "orders" (the cart drawer stays available in both). The Checkout button's handler now builds an OrderDraft from cart.items (mapping each CartLine to an OrderLine via product.id/name/price and qty, with a fixed demo Address and PaymentMethod since no address/payment form exists), calls useOrders().place(draft), and calls cart.clear() only after place resolves.

acceptance.text: App still compiles and default-exports a zero-arg component; no existing import from src/products.ts or src/cart.ts is removed or changed in a way that breaks their current signatures.
With view === "store" (the initial state), the product grid, hero and cart drawer render exactly as before this change.
